races.title: State Senate, District 38
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Laura Bassett
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 38. Licensed real estate professional since 2003 and licensed professional fiduciary since 2011. Owns two local businesses in real estate and fiduciary services. USC accounting graduate. Serves as a San Diego County Civil Service Commissioner.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed on Ballotpedia)

cands.gaps: Laura Bassett has held no elected office, so there is no voting record. Her birthplace is not stated, only that she is a lifelong Oceanside resident. We found no documented actions in office or filings on data centers, homestead property tax, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice. Her campaign site does not say where she stands on these issues. Her site backs 'responsible development' and local control over state housing mandates, but it has no dated statement on data centers or development that we could cite. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no news coverage or controversies about her.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she is a lifelong Oceanside resident who grew up there and raised six children there, but it does not give her birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Founded and operates two businesses in real estate and fiduciary services. Licensed real estate professional since 2003 and professional fiduciary since 2011. Holds a USC accounting degree (1989). Has held no elected office.
qual.why: A business owner and manager with finance and fiduciary experience falls in the middle band. She has no legislative service or elected office, and her county commission seat and chamber ambassador role add nothing under the rubric.
qual.label: A business owner and manager with finance and fiduciary experience falls in the middle band. She has no legislative service or elected office, and her county commission seat and chamber ambassador role add nothing under the rubric.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she supports law enforcement and stronger consequences for serious and repeat offenders, and that Sacramento should fully fund Proposition 36.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she is a lifelong Oceanside resident who grew up there and raised six children there, but it does not give her birthplace.

cands.name: Catherine S. Blakespear
cands.bio: California State Senator for District 38 since December 2022. Attorney and former journalist (Los Angeles Times, Associated Press). Former Encinitas traffic commissioner, city councilmember (elected 2014) and three-term mayor. Chairs the Senate Environmental Quality Committee.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter, among others listed for her 2026 race.
Sierra Club California, per her campaign site.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was raised or when she settled in the San Diego area, though she was born in Encinitas. We found no documented stance from her on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, or school choice and teacher pay. The deeds on her campaign site are her own claims, and we did not verify them against legislative records. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The pages gave no reporting on controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says she was born in Encinitas and lives there, and her campaign site calls her a fourth-generation San Diegan, but neither says where she grew up; the record shows her in Encinitas public life from her 2014 council election, about 12 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has been a California state senator since 2022 and sits on the Budget and Fiscal Review Committee. Earlier she was Encinitas mayor and councilmember (council from 2014), an attorney at Ray Quinney & Nebeker, and a journalist for the Los Angeles Times and Associated Press.
qual.why: Prior and current legislative service and a law background, plus local elected office, put her in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.
qual.label: Prior and current legislative service and a law background, plus local elected office, put her in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she authored legislation requiring people in mental health crises to turn in their firearms and co-authored bills to toughen enforcement of California's Red Flag laws.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she is "100% pro-choice, 100% of the time" and is rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says she closed developer loopholes used to circumvent local zoning and expanded wildlife habitat and open space through continued state conservation funding.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she works "shoulder-to-shoulder with law enforcement," wants gun crimes prosecuted to the fullest extent, and sped up encampment removals.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised
